utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the number of men involved?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what their number was, because Muslim refugees had arrived from Jajce, and Vinac, who stayed with our Muslims, and that's why I couldn't say how many there were, because there was a big Muslim house, and in this house alone there were 30 refugees from Jajce. That was when they were driven out by the Serbs. So that it was said that they brought a lot of weapons with them, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you say, during the fighting in Gacice on the 20th of April, was anyone killed or wounded either on the Croatian or the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I heard that a young man had been killed on the Croatian side, that his name was Marko and he was a refugee from Dobratici. And on the Muslim side I heard that one of their soldiers had been killed by a shell, and one was hit by a bullet at the way out of the village, and one burned to death in his house. And I heard that one was killed by the Muslims because he started fleeing during the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were any of them civilians or were they all soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: They were all soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were any civilians killed or wounded after they were taken to Vitez and returned to Gacice?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You also said that you know that in a number of Muslim houses there were refugees?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of military organisation they had in the village? Do you know or not?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether they had radio transmitters?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: They found radio transmitter or, rather, a man found a radio transmitter in the Muslim village after the fighting and he found a list or a kind of record which I saw. It was handwritten. And then they sent the radio transmitter to our police station and we were told by the police then that there should be another smaller radio transmitter, and that was found at the other end of the village in a manhole.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where the radio transmitter was found?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: The radio transmitter was found in the house of Sadik Hrustic, one of them. That was the bigger radio transmitter with the piece of paper next to it. And the other one was found at the other end of the village in a manhole in front of the house of Mesud Hrustic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Both houses belonged to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have completed my part of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Counsel Radovic going to -- no? All right. Thank you. Any other Defence counsel prepared to cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: The other counsel do not intend to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I see Mr. Smith is going to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise to Judge May, I can't see you behind the pole, but that's how this set-up is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Ms. Matic, I appear on behalf of the Prosecution. My name is Bill Smith. I appear with Mr. Franck Terrier, Mr. Michael Blaxill, and it's my role to ask you a few questions about the testimony you've given today. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that in the village of Gacice there was about 200 Muslims and 200 Croats living there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after that 15 days that a large number of Muslims were taken away. How many Muslims were left in the village after the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: On the 16th of April all the Muslims were in the village because on the 16th of April nothing was going on in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, my question is slightly confused. After the attack, after the fighting in Gacice on the 20th of April, you stated that during that day that a group of men escaped from the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: A group of men escaping from the village? No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you said some soldiers escaped from the village and went to Krusica.

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Oh, soldiers. Yes, all the Muslim soldiers left and I saw a group of Muslims with a white flag, and up to then I had heard that all the Muslims in the upper part of the village had gone to Krusica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And those Muslims were men that lived in the village, the ones that escaped to Krusica; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the group of men that had some rifles, some guns; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that group was about 40 in size, approximately 40 men?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, because, as I said, there were a lot of refugees from Jajce who also had weapons and who had brought weapons and fought. So I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many people in Gacice had weapons before the attack on the 20th of April? Sorry, about how many Muslim men had weapons?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I put it to you that 40, about 40 Muslim men had weapons, and they came from the village. Do you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In any event, the main part of the Muslim defence or the Muslim soldiers, they in fact escaped leaving the rest of the people in the village, largely women and children and a few men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And those -- I think the number is about 247. About 250 people, women and children and men, some men, were taken to Vitez. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I said that they were taken to Vitez. One group passed by my house and the other group I couldn't see because they came out at the bottom of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said the village had about 200 Muslims living in it and -- I withdraw the question. Those people went to Vitez, that large group, you stated that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What was the purpose of them going to Vitez? Why were they taken there?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you hear later that they were taken to the Hotel Vitez, taken out the front of the Hotel Vitez and kept there for about two or three hours?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: The front of the hotel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was shelling in the area of the Hotel Vitez on the 20th of April, shelling by the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware that the reason why they were taken to the Hotel Vitez was to protect the main headquarters of the HVO from the Muslim shelling using that group of people, that 250 people, as a human shield to protect the HVO headquarter staff?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, I don't know this, and the Muslims were brought back quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So you've got no idea why they were taken to the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said they were taken back to the village of Gacice. Who took them back to Gacice?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know that either. Probably one of the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: One of the Croats from the village or a Croat from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And they were kept in some Muslim houses in the village closer towards Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, closer to Vitez, at the beginning of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Why didn't they go back to their own houses?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I think that our people kept them in those few houses for some kind of security because there were unknown people, the army had started moving around, so to protect them. But in the daytime they moved about freely. They went back to their houses, fed their livestock, worked, and maybe they themselves wanted to stay together for safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: (Microphone not activated) -- were guarded by HVO soldiers, this group of Muslims in these houses?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: At night people from the village kept guard in front of the houses or, in fact, along the road where the houses were next to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many Croats from the village kept guard on these Muslims at night?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Two respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know the names of these guards?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I do not know the names of all the guards, but I saw Boro Krizanovic and Ratko Matic, whose nickname was Ride. They kept guard on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And these Muslims were kept in about seven houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And a large number of them --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And a large number of the Muslims couldn't go back to their houses because they were destroyed in the attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, around ten houses were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that the village of Gacice was divided into two basic parts, the Muslim part, which was purely Muslim, and then there was a mixed part of the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the Muslim part of the village is the upper part of the village; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, the Muslim part of the village or, rather, a part of the village that is closer to this factory of ours and around the centre of the village there are Croat and Muslim houses, for example, by the road are Croat houses. That's where my house is too, all the way to the bottom of the village. And that is where there are mixed Croat and Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say the bottom of the village, you mean closer towards Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No. When I say "above the village," I mean above the purely Muslim part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can show you a map of the village, a photograph, an aerial photograph which -- it's an enlarged version of that large map, that aerial photograph that you see behind you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 350.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mrs. Matic, it would help me, and I think it would help the Court to understand your testimony further by looking at this aerial photograph that's placed on the ELMO just next to you. Looking at that photograph, does that look familiar to you? Can you orientate yourself around that map in relation to where the purely Muslim part of the village is in Gacice?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I'm not very good with maps. However, everything would be clear to me if you would show me where the road from Vitez to the village is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you look at the figure number 4, the road just below that, if you go left off the map, that road leads to Vitez. And just below the figure number 4, I think you see a large elongated building that's adjacent to the road. That is the local community centre for Gacice. And if you move further to the right towards the figure number 5, you will see that large area below the figure number 5 with a large number of houses that have been destroyed, houses or barns and sheds. I think you can see on the photograph the roofs, the roofs of these places missing. And the number 5 area is an area in the village where mainly Croats live. I believe it's the Krizanovics where that large group of families lived. And if you look at the figure number 2, that is an area where some Muslim houses are. You can see from that figure number 2 that it appears that none of those houses have been destroyed. If you look towards the bottom of the photograph, the right-hand corner, you will see a large building. And that's part of the Slobodan Princip Seljo factory, the munitions factory between Donja Veceriska and Gacice. That's just the start of the factory. And if you look at the map where the figure 4 can be seen, on the other side of the road to that, below that, that area was the general area that the Muslims that were taken to Hotel Vitez were housed over that 15 days. Does that description help you orientate yourself around this map?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: (Indicating) This is the road from Vitez leading to the village. If you said that this building is the local community centre --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mrs. Matic. It's difficult, I know, but if you could point us to these locations on the ELMO. Unfortunately, that doesn't come up on everyone's screen.

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: This is the road from Vitez, right. I'm not very good with these maps at all. What did you say? This was the community centre, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The building just below the number 4 is the community centre in Gacice. There is a community centre in Gacice, Mrs. Matic, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that community centre is alongside the main road into the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that community centre is in the mixed part of the village?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you go along that road from number 4 to area number 5, you are moving forward away from Vitez. And that area where the number 1 is, is that not the purely Muslim part of the village, and then just above that, where the number 5 is, is that not the Croat area where the Krizanovics, a large number of their families live?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I am having such a lot of trouble with this map. Well, perhaps that is right. Perhaps that is the Muslim centre of the village, the purely Muslim part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mrs. Krizanovic -- Mrs. Matic, I apologise. I don't want you to guess. Can you tell the Court whether the -- you may want to sit down now. Can you tell the Court whether there are a group of families that live in Gacice that are called the Krizanovics?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many families in that village with the name of Krizanovic?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: About ten houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And those houses are right next to the purely Muslim part of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In fact, the area where the Krizanovics live is surrounded by Muslim houses, one the centre of the village and one where that figure 2 is, that area further away from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: The Krizanovic houses are close to this Muslim centre of the village and on one side of the Krizanovic houses there are Muslim houses too, but then on the other side there are no houses any more. There are only meadows, pastures, and then the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the Krizanovics live at the outer most point of the village, the furthest away point from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is the upper part of the village. That is the very end of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I think you stated -- actually, I can't remember accurately. About how many Croat houses were destroyed in the village as a result of this attack?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: One house burnt down completely. Two houses burnt down in part. Two barns, two sheds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many people live in the purely Muslim part of Gacice? Can you give an estimate of that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: My estimate is -- well, I already said that approximately half of the village population was Croat and the other half was Muslim. And then in the Muslim part, half of it was purely Muslim and the other half roughly was mixed with Croat houses too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you stated about 200 people lived, 200 Muslims lived in Gacice?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Half of them lived in the purely Muslim part, and if you look at that map in front of you now, do you agree with me now that the area covered by figure number 1 is the purely Muslim part of the village, in light of what you've said?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You stated in your evidence that there are about ten houses that were destroyed in this attack, and you said that there was one further house that was destroyed at a later time. If you look at the area marked with number 1, there are quite a large number of houses and barns and sheds in that area. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I said that about ten buildings were set fire to in the fighting, but I also said that some of the Muslim houses were very, very old in the Muslim part of the village and during the war they were shelled and heavy guns were used. It's the Muslims who were actually shooting at the Croat part from Zabrdje, from Preocica, and sometimes, accidentally, they would hit some of their own houses, and then later on, because of the inclimate weather conditions, especially during the winter, they would fall apart. But there were also some empty houses, because some people built new houses in that part of the village where they lived together with the Croats. So they already did have some houses that were abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So are you saying now that more houses were damaged in the village after the attack on the 20th of April, more houses than the ten that you originally stated?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No. No. No. These houses were, perhaps, photographed a year later, as I said. They started falling apart themselves. But I said that during the fighting ten Muslim houses burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The others just fell apart of their own accord?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I said the others were hit by shells or some other kind of weapon, and I said that these houses were made of mud, and then if there was a hole in the roof, yes, it would fall apart. Because nobody repaired them during that one year. For example, I was staying at my house and I repaired it during the summer. These houses, as soon as anything would happen to them, they would crumble.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's quarter past 12. I am wondering if it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Shall we take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, may I ask you if you have many more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, about 20 minutes worth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you maybe concentrate on major issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Ms. Matic, you mentioned that you saw some Muslim villagers destroying two or three houses on the 20th of April. What were their names again?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: They were -- two of them were sons of Hamdija Ramulj. I don't know their names exactly and the other was the son of Avdo Hercerg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You were in a position to identify them on that day?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you knew them because they grew up in the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And prior to that day had they shown any behaviour that was of such a criminal nature?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how old were these people?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: They were perhaps about 25 to 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was it a surprise to you that you saw them destroying these houses on this day because they hadn't shown that type of behaviour beforehand?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm not sure whether you said in your testimony today, but in your testimony in the -- in another case before the Tribunal, you stated that you were also shot at on the 20th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to who was involved in this attack or this fighting in the village, is it fair to say that the local Croat village guard was involved in the defence or the attack of the village, as well as a group called the Vitezovi, and as well as some military police from the HVO? Those three groups, is it fair to say that those three groups were involved in the fighting in the village?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Since on that day it was impossible to go outside, I don't know exactly how many people from the village were involved, but when I saw the group of soldiers who said, "Left wing forward, victory is ours," then the Muslims appeared very fast with the white flag and I heard that they were the Vitezovi or the Knights.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But the village guards were also involved in the attack as well, do you agree? At least some of them.

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many of the local village guards would you say were involved in the fighting in the village?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, the local village guard, were they in the HVO? Were they a part of the HVO reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So the local village guard was working with the Vitezovi in the defence of this village, or attack of the village, whichever way you look at it?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It was a joint effort?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: After the 16 days that the Muslims -- the women and children that were kept in these seven houses in the village, they were taken by truck to Dubravica. Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I heard that some trucks had arrived to pick them up and they left in the direction of Zenica, and that's all I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you hear that these people -- this group of about 200 were taken to near Dubravica and taken off the truck, and told to walk through the frontlines and to walk to Zenica? Did you hear that particular fact?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that Anto Krizanovic was elected on the 16th of April to negotiate with the Muslim defence in the village. You remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Anto Krizanovic was in fact -- he was the commander of the village guards prior to the 16th of April, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So if I say to you that Anto Krizanovic was commander of the village guard from about May '92 onwards, you wouldn't be able to dispute that, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, questions are being asked twice. The witness has already responded to this question, that she doesn't know. The question is not so important, but some leading questions are being asked in a way I feel is inadmissible because really, the witness responds and then another answer is suggested to her. So please do not allow Mr. Smith to ask questions in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I feel I must sustain this objection. Mr. Smith, could you move on and ask questions which are not leading and also not repetitive?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In relation to cross-examination, Your Honour, there are a number of places where I do need to ask leading questions. However, I do understand that the last question was repetitive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: During the period prior to the fighting in Gacice, you mentioned that there were negotiations between Anto Krizanovic and the commander of the Muslim village guard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Anto Krizanovic had been called to Vitez, to the HVO headquarters in Vitez, after the 16th of April and was spoken to by commanders of the HVO to organise that the Muslims hand over their weapons. Are you aware that Anto Krizanovic did that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware that the village guard, the village guard in Gacice, communicated with the HVO headquarters even prior to the 16th of April in some of the military matters of the village?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: As regards military questions and the war itself in our area, if I had known that negotiations were going on, I think I would not have -- and my children went to Germany. They were refugees in Germany. I wouldn't have brought my children back to the village on the 24th if I had known, because it would have been a crime against my own children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you brought your family back to Gacice in what month?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: On the 10th I brought them back and the war started in our village on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that the reason why the village guard separated was because some weapons were stolen by the Muslims and taken to another place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the main incident that caused the separation in the guards?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember -- sorry, I withdraw that. Boro Krizanovic shot Besim Subasic prior to this attack on the 16th of April, and Boro Krizanovic is a resident of Gacice; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, Boro Krizanovic lives in Gacice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you tell the court who Besim Subasic is?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Besim Subasic lived in Gacice as well, but before the war he built a new house between the village of Gacice and Kamenjace and he lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you hear that Boro Krizanovic shot him and wounded him prior to the 16th of April, in late '92?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Since Boro Krizanovic likes to drink alcohol, I heard that there had been some incidents between them, but whether he was wounded on that occasion or not I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Since the fighting in Gacice did you ever hear about what had happened in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm not talking about this particular court case, but shortly after, say in the month of May '93, did you hear about what happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I heard that the conflict started there first and that there were a lot of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you hear who the victims belonged to and whether they were soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I only heard that they were Muslims, but whether they were civilians or soldiers I don't know. It was quite far away from where I was and there wasn't much movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The fighting in the village on the 20th of April was an attack by HVO forces and the forces that we mentioned earlier, the Vitezovi, and the local village guard. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No. First of all, I don't know who started shooting first, whether it was started by the Croats or the Muslims, because after the clashes, when they found the radio transmitter and the piece of paper, it said that the Muslims would attack the Croats at half past seven, and that they would get help at half past nine. So I don't know who attacked, and I can't know because I was not outdoors, and I couldn't have been outdoors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were three houses in the village, Croat houses in the village that were destroyed or set on fire, and you explained to the Court who the people were that, actually, you assumed, set alight to those houses. Were there any other Croat houses shelled in the village?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: That day, when there was fighting, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in the mixed part of the village there were some Muslim houses that were destroyed as well, do you agree, on that day?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you say, Ms. Matic, with regard to the houses that you mentioned in that part of the village, the old part of the village which were there, you said that they were built out of some kind of mud. What kind of material is that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: It's a kind of brick made of clay, made of earth, and it is dried in the sun for about a month, and they used those bricks to build those old houses. Five or six of those houses were abandoned before the war because people had built new houses and moved out of those houses, so they were already very dilapidated. They were very old and rundown, and the walls made of those bricks were -- only some of them were recent, but the old part of the village was all built of adobe bricks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that the picture you can see was not taken then but that the photograph was made later?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, much later, that's certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You also said that you had to repair your own house, replace the window panes and so on because of shelling, and that other houses had been damaged.

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, and there is still damage to other houses and my own house, but we had to put new window panes in. In my house for example, a part of my roof was damaged. Of course, I had to replace the roof tiles. But some part is still damaged. For example, the chimney that belongs to the central heating, which is next to the house, that is still destroyed. It still hasn't been repaired. There is no house without any damage to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did the shelling come later in '93 'til '94; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, every day. Every day. Regardless whether it was because of this factory, I don't know, I just know that every day there were shells, there were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And, tell me, what Mr. Smith showed to you, that part, that is where the SPS factory starts; is that correct? Could you please look at the aerial image once again. The part that is in the lower right-hand part, is that the SPS factory?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And that part of the village close to the SPS factory was shelled by the Muslim side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: All right. Please tell the Court, who did you see that day? I am referring to soldiers. You mentioned the Vitezovi, right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Are those the only members of the military you saw that day?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who are the Vitezovi otherwise?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this to you. The Vitezovi were some kind of an organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Those weren't people from the village, right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, no, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I heard that Darko Kraljevic was their commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the Vitezovi were primarily from Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The men that you saw, these Vitezovi, when you heard that order, was any one of the local villagers amongst them?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see? Can you tell us how many Vitezovi, how many soldiers you saw?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Well, I saw about 20 men. First of all, I did not dare go out. I could not go out. And what I saw briefly, as I glanced through the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the only soldiers that you saw in this battle on that particular day were the Vitezovi on the Croat side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: One more thing, please. On several occasions you were asked about this. Do you know how many people were there in the village and how many people were in these houses that were taken to Vitez and then taken back? Do you know how many people had fled before that?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: I don't know. I know how many local Muslims there were in the village, but I do not know the exact number who left before that. And also I don't know because of the refugees, so I cannot exactly tell you in exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And my last question. Do you know how many soldiers there were in the village? You said perhaps 40. Do you know how many Muslim soldiers left? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you do not know the number?

utterances.speaker: Andelka Matic
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have concluded my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No questions from the Court. Mrs. Matic, thank you so much for giving evidence in Court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESSE
utterances.text: Now, before we move onto our next witness, I understand -- sorry, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would just like to tender the exhibit, Prosecution 350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. No objection, so P350 is admitted into evidence. I understand the Defence have requested protective measures for the next witness. If there is no objection from the Prosecution, they are granted. So we will move into closed session, I understand. So while we prepare for moving into closed session, may I discuss briefly with you a few points raised by the Prosecutor in their motion filed on the 5th of February. Just to remind the Defence counsel that they are requested to answer the various points raised by the Prosecutor. First of all, the item number 2 in that motion, namely, they should specify that the Defence counsel are not intending to call those witnesses who are listed there on page 2 and 3 and 4 of that motion under item 2. I wonder whether this can be clarified by Defence counsel. Number 3, again the Prosecutor wishes to know whether the list of four expert witnesses is the only list of expert witnesses the Defence intend to call. Number 4, whether Defence counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic still intends to call the geometrist Kesic. I hope Counsel Krajina will let us know his position. Now, item 5, the Prosecutor is requesting summaries for -- or the statements relating to the five witnesses listed there. I hope Defence counsel will be prepared to pass onto the Prosecutor and to the Court those summaries. Then the final point covered in item 6 and 7. It's about the insufficient information submitted by Defence counsel concerning the witnesses listed on page 6, 7 and 8 of this motion. Now, we have discussed this matter and we feel that the Defence counsel must provide sufficiently detailed summaries of witness statements. If they don't, the logical consequence will be that in the examination-in-chief, the cross-examination will be confined to those specific points raised in the existing summary statements. So we will not allow any examination or cross-examination on other points, points other than those covered in those summary statements. So therefore I call up on Defence counsel, as I say, to provide detailed statements for those witnesses, given that the Prosecutor has convincingly shown that they are not in a position to interview those witnesses, as explained in paragraph 6 of their motion. All right. I wonder if -- well, I hope that Defence counsel may be in a position to give us all this information by, say, by Friday. Good. All right. So let us move onto our next witness. Yes, Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: May I just comment on this briefly. I don't want to keep the Court too long. We can respond already at this stage as to whether we are going to call in as an expert witness Bladzan Kesic, a geometrist. I wish to confirm that we shall call him. So this list of expert witnesses is five altogether. All of them were proposed to be witnesses by Vlatko Kupreskic's counsel, so indeed we are going to call all of them. In connection with a request that we got from the Prosecutor, we intend to write a letter to the Prosecutor stating our views on each and every one of these items. And after that, if the Prosecutor has some concrete questions, he can address us directly before the Court. We have adopted this view for the following reason: We have discussed these matters on several occasions here in Court and we also had a concrete agreement with the Prosecutor himself and with The Office of the Prosecutor with regard to each and every one of the witnesses. And we said that we agreed to give supplementary information concerning certain witnesses. Then the Court instructed us to give additional information as regards the President of the Supreme Court. And now again we are being given an additional request with regard to the witnesses concerning which we said then that they would not be questioned about anything that is outside their original witness statements. So this had already been agreed upon once --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry. I see the witness is standing there. Could you conclude, because otherwise the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I shall conclude. I shall. I shall. So we, as Vlatko Kupreskic's Defence counsel, we shall address the Prosecutor in a letter with regard to these questions that are considered to be controversial, and then, if there is anything controversial left, we shall discuss it here in Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.
